title: Automated blue/green replay-and-heal rollout with session-aware canaries
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds an automated replay-and-heal executor for blue/green rollouts. New safety gates: session-aware canary sampling, deterministic replay harness, and audit-backed rollback. Backwards compatible with existing rollout policies.
description:
Motivation: We observed several canary failures where transient infra flakiness or external API hiccups caused noisy metric signals and unnecessary rollbacks. This PR implements an automated 'replay-and-heal' step for blue/green promotions: when a canary batch trips metric failure thresholds, the platform will optionally (configurable per-rollout) pause, capture the failing canary traffic snapshot, and replay it deterministically against the previous stable variant and against an isolated replay harness to identify whether the failure is reproducible or transient. If the replay shows non-deterministic failures (i.e. stable variant succeeds or errors don't reproduce), the rollout resumes with an automated "heal" path that can: 1) clear transient cache/connection buckets, 2) retry canary at reduced weight, or 3) perform a targeted rollback with snapshot auditing. Key features: - Session-aware canaries: traffic sampling preserves session-affinity groups to avoid mixing stateful sessions across variants. - Deterministic replay harness: recorded requests, headers, and session keys are replayed in the same order with preserved timing window metadata to improve reproducibility. - Replay comparison policy: configurable similarity metrics (latency delta, error-class match, token-level divergence for LLM outputs) with pluggable thresholds. - Audit trail: all replays, snapshots and decisions are written to the rollout ledger and exposed in Console for post-mortem. - Minimal infra impact: replay jobs run on isolated pod pool with capped concurrency and token-cost budget. - Backwards compatibility: rollout manifests gain an optional 'replay_heal' block; existing rollouts default to off.

What this PR changes (summary): 1) rollout/engine: add ReplayHealExecutor with state machine states {RUN_CANARY, PAUSE_CAPTURE, RUN_REPLAY, ANALYZE, HEAL_OR_ROLLBACK, PROMOTE}. 2) rollout/api: extend rollout schema with 'replay_heal' stanza and new validation. 3) runtime: session-affinity sampler and deterministic request recorder. 4) console: new UI timeline entry and buttons for manual replay/force-heal. 5) tests: end-to-end canary replay flow tests and unit tests for comparison heuristics.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-3412). - [x] Unit tests added for executor transitions and comparison logic. - [x] E2E smoke harness added (flaky on first run, rerun fixed). - [x] Console timeline elements implemented and behind feature flag. - [x] Documentation stub in docs/rollouts/replay-heal.md.

review_comments: Evan Cho (Reviewer): Nice clear state machine. Two asks: (1) ensure we cap token budget per replay job and surface that in the manifest; (2) move deterministic recorder to runtime/recorder package to make it reusable by other features.

Priya Menon (Author): Addressed both in subsequent commits: added 'replay_budget_tokens' to manifest proto with validation and moved recorder implementation to runtime/recorder. Updated docs to call out limits.
Lena García (Reviewer): Tests look good. The e2e was flaky on first CI run — can you add retry logic to the harness and an assertion about audit entries being created?
Priya Menon (Author): Added retry for the harness and asserts for ledger entries in tests; pushed new commit. CI reran and passed.

Marcus Holt (Reviewer): Concern about auto-heal producing inconsistent user-visible outputs for LLM responses. Suggest we expose an opt-in policy per rollout for 'strict_output_match' which forces rollback on divergence. If not opted-in, heal path may proceed conservatively.
Priya Menon (Author): Added 'strict_output_match' boolean to replay_heal policy; default false to preserve existing behavior. Updated comparison thresholds and docs.
Lena García (Approver): Approving after tests green and policy flag added. (LGTM)
